textbookText: Symbiotic 3.1.8 Mode of nutrition in bacteria

1. Autotrophic Bacteria A small group of bacteria show autotrophic nutrition. The bacteria that synthesize their own organic food from inorganic substances are called autotrophic bacteria. They utilize sunlight or chemical energy as a source of energy. Autotrophic bacteria are of two types:

a. Photoautotrophic bacteria: These bacteria utilize light energy to perform photosynthesis process. However, bacterial photosynthesis is different from green plant photosynthesis because water is not utilized as hydrogen donor so, oxygen is not evolved. This process is called anoxygenic photosynthesis. Instead of water they utilize hydrogen sulphide (H2S), thiosulphate, hydrogen or other organic compounds.

These bacteria utilize chemical energy to convert inorganic compound to organic compound and this process is called as chemosynthesis. They get energy from ammonia, nitrate, nitrite, ferrous iron, hydrogen sulphides and other inorganic compounds for the synthesis of their food. On the basis of chemical compounds they use as a source of energy, chemoautotrophic bacteria are grouped as nitrifying bacteria (utilize ammonia or nitrate), Sulphur bacteria (utilize Hydrogen sulphide), Iron bacteria (utilize ferrous compound), Hydrogen bacteria (utilize hydrogen), methane bacteria (utilize methane) etc.

2. Heterotrophic Bacteria These are the bacteria which are unable to synthesize their organic food. They depend on other organisms for their nutrition. Most of the bacteria show heterotrophic mode of nutrition. Heterotrophic bacteria are of three types –

a. Saprophytic bacteria: The bacteria that obtain their nutrition from dead and decaying organic matter are called saprophytic bacteria. These bacteria breakdown the complex organic matter into simpler forms by secreting different types of digestive enzymes. The bacteria play an important role in the recycling of nutrients by decomposition. So, they are also called natural scavengers. They are the decomposers of an ecosystem. Some examples are: Pseudomonas, Acetobacter, Clostridium, etc.

b. Parasitic bacteria: The parasitic bacteria obtain their nutrition from living cell of other organisms. The parasitic bacteria may cause diseases (pathogenic) like Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Clostridium tetani, and Salmonella typhi.

c. Symbiotic bacteria: The bacteria that live in close association with other organism in such a way that both the partners get mutual benefit from this association are called symbiotic bacteria. Example: Rhizobium bacteria present in the root nodules of leguminous plant, Escherichia coli in the human intestine.
